content_of_post_to_answer: Does living in a modern city make people more mentally fragile than their ancestors were?
answer: Cities may not make people more fragile; they often make people more aware of fragility. Ancestors faced harsher physical conditions, but many struggles were immediate and unavoidable. Modern life removes many threats while exposing us to constant comparison, uncertainty, and abstract pressures. I’ve explored this pattern in more detail on my profile for those interested in the psychological tradeoffs of modern living. Comfort can reduce resilience, but awareness can also create the chance to build a different kind of strength.
